content:
The test image shows a tomato plant with:
- Mosaic/mottled pattern of light and dark green/yellow on leaves
- Irregular yellow-green patches throughout the canopy
- Some leaf distortion/malformation
- No distinct necrotic spots, no powdery coating, no water-soaked lesions

This strongly suggests a viral disease — the mosaic and mottling pattern is classic for Cucumber Mosaic Virus. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference CMV image shows severe shoestring leaf malformation and mosaic mottling — a more advanced case. The test image shows the characteristic mosaic pattern (alternating light/dark green and yellow patches) with moderate leaf distortion, consistent with an earlier or milder CMV infection.

Key matches to CMV:
- Mosaic/mottled light and dark green/yellow pattern across leaves
- Irregular yellowing on younger leaves
- Mild leaf distortion
- No necrotic spots (rules out TSWV), no powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew), no distinct lesions (rules out Early/Late Blight, Septoria)
